# Estimate Analysis

⚠️ **Trading warning / Avertissement trading** : informational only, not investment advice. Estimate revisions are a signal about expectations, not a guarantee of future results. Curated by Skill Harbor: a deep dive into analyst estimates and, above all, into how they are moving. It presents the current EPS and revenue consensus for every available period (current quarter, next quarter, current year, next year) with the low and high range, the range width as a share of consensus, and the analyst count, then tracks the revision trend: each period's estimate today versus 7, 30, 60, and 90 days ago, with attention to whether the recent moves are accelerating. It counts revision breadth (how many analysts raised versus cut, and the up ratio), compares expected growth with the industry, the sector, and the S&P 500, and grades the estimates themselves against the last four quarters of actual results, because a consensus with a poor track record deserves less trust. Routes run from a narrow question (just the revision trend) to the full picture. Data comes from Yahoo Finance through the free yfinance library. From the himself65/finance-skills repository (MIT). Honest caveats: you need Python 3 with pip (the skill installs yfinance itself if missing); Yahoo Finance estimates can lag professional real-time consensus feeds by hours or days; estimates cluster around the consensus, so real outcomes scatter wider than the low to high range suggests; next-year estimates are the least...
